chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from 'Amr ibn 'Uthman, from Muhammad ibn 'Uthafar, from one of his companions, from Muhammad ibn Muslim or Abu Hamza, from Abu Abdillah, from his father (peace be upon them), who said:

Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O my son! Watch out for five, so do not accompany them, nor converse with them, nor travel with them on a road.' I said: 'O father! Who are they?' He said: 'Beware of accompanying the liar, for he is like a mirage; he brings the distant near to you and distances the near from you.'
And beware of accompanying the immoral, for he would sell you for a meal or less than that.
And beware of accompanying the stingy, for he would abandon you regarding his wealth when you are most in need of it.
And beware of accompanying the stupid, for he intends to benefit you but actually harms you.
And beware of accompanying the severer of his kinship ties, for I found him to be cursed in the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in three places.

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'So what is the matter with you that, if you took command, you would surely make mischief in the land and cut off your ties of kinship? Those it is whom Allah has cursed, so He has made them deaf and blinded their eyes.'

And He said: 'Those who break the covenant of Allah after its confirmation and sever what Allah has commanded to be joined and cause mischief in the land; those are the ones who have the curse, and for them is the evil abode.'
And He said in Surah Al-Baqarah: 'Those who break the covenant of Allah after its confirmation and sever what Allah has commanded to be joined and cause mischief in the land; those are the losers.'
ai.seo_question: What are the five types of people one should avoid befriending according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin) outlines five distinct character flaws that corrupt social and spiritual life, ranging from the deceptive nature of the liar to the well-meaning but harmful impact of the fool. He specifically emphasizes the severer of kinship ties (*qati' al-rahim*) by citing three Quranic verses to demonstrate that this trait incurs a divine curse, linking social ethics directly to scriptural authority. This teaching underscores the Shia emphasis on selecting companions based on moral integrity (*akhlaq*) as a means of preserving one's own faith and social standing.
